alt: Clean turquoise pool with paver coping beside a large home

problems: A adds a foreground pool edge or coping strip along the bottom that does not exist in B. It is stained with rust-colored patches and has a drain or light fixture on it.
The bottom-left of B shows only water and a small bit of coping, so A's foreground structure is an extra object and changes the scene layout.
The reflections in A are blocky and pixelated, with hard-edged dark shapes that look like AI artifacts. They are not natural reflections of the house.
The green algae and leaves in A look painted on. Parts of the algae seem to rise above the water line near the right edge.
The water in A has an unnatural split. One half is clean turquoise and the other half is murky green, with a sharp boundary and no consistent lighting.
A shows the pool's tile line and waterline on the right side as clear water over a visible tile edge, but the tile line is partly hidden by algae, so it doesn't match B.
The foreground tiles in A have blotchy, smeared patches of discoloration that look unrealistic.
A leaves out the yellow duck toy floating in B. This is minor, but the objects in the scene differ.
The green algae patch has hard, blocky, pixelated edges. It looks like a pasted mask and not natural algae spreading in water.
Clear turquoise rectangular blocks sit inside the green area, for example at the lower left, the bottom center and a small square near the bottom right. These look like leftover unedited patches.
The dark green region has reflections of the house and columns that look like dark silhouettes. They don't match the lighting in B.
The leaves and sticks on the water look scattered and artificial, with a flat, plastic texture.
The water ripple and caustic pattern does not blend between the clear and green areas. The transition looks abrupt.
The yellow rubber duck visible in B is missing from A. This is a minor difference.
The surrounding scene (deck, fence, lifebuoy, shrubs, pool edge) matches B and has no warping.
